9:41

You order, a pro handles it

Pick a service and pay. A certified DRON operator does the flying — you never touch the drone.

A verified, insured operator

The moment you pay you see their name, photo and live position. Someone accountable is on the way.

What the drone does — and doesn't

It flies a set route, keeps its distance, and only records what your order needs. Brief low noise on take-off and landing; no filming of your neighbours.

Banner messageThe banner message is the empty state that carries a picture: an illustrated top, the sentence, and one way out.

Payment received

Your operator is on the way.

OutcomeThe outcome is the success screen, and success is deliberately rare: only the screens where the job has a result earn one, such as order-confirmed (Payment received), inspection-report (Report ready) and resolution (Refund issued), plus the loading screens while the money or the check moves.
SkeletonA skeleton is a claim about the loaded screen: it rehearses that screen's layout at its exact size, so nothing moves when the content arrives.
Link copied.
ToastA toast is a transient confirmation for an action that finishes on the screen you are standing on and leaves no other trace.

Media 2

Media wellThe well holds the product's real imagery: drone renders, scenes, the operator's delivery photo and the live map, never illustration and never a gradient.
Photo pileSeveral photographs from one order, shown the way a phone shows several photographs: a loose pile, not a grid.
